sections.name: File setup (part 1)
sections.title: Database and cache containers
sections.what: Starts Postgres with vector support and Redis, each with a health check and saved data storage.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app needs a database and a fast cache during development.
sections.watch_out: Postgres uses a fixed, weak password and should only be reachable from the developer's own machine.

sections.name: File setup (part 2)
sections.title: File storage and OCR service
sections.what: Starts MinIO, a one-time bucket setup container, and the OCR service with its source folder mounted so edits show up live.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the names.
sections.watch_out: The bucket is made publicly downloadable and the setup step always reports success. The storage key names here differ from the names in the example environment file.

sections.name: File setup (part 3)
sections.title: AI service and job dashboard
sections.what: Starts the AI service with its database and cache addresses and the OpenAI key taken from the environment. Also starts a web dashboard for background jobs.
sections.why: Likely reason: the dashboard lets a developer see queued background jobs.
sections.watch_out: The AI service hardcodes its database address and password, so changing the environment file will not change them.

summary: Starts the local development stack: a Postgres database, a Redis cache, MinIO file storage, the OCR and AI Python services, and a background job dashboard.
purpose: Lets a developer run all supporting services on their own computer with one command.
why: Likely reason: keeps the local setup the same for everyone and avoids installing each service by hand.
how: Each service is defined with an image or a build folder, its ports, environment settings, and a health check. Services that depend on others wait until those are healthy. A setup container creates the default file bucket.
inputs: Environment variables from the shell, the database setup SQL file, and the source folders of the OCR and AI services.
risks: Credentials are fixed and weak, such as postgres with postgres and minioadmin. The MinIO bucket is set to public download, so anyone who can guess a file name can read it. The setup container exits with success even when it fails, which hides errors. Debug logging is on. This file is for local development only.
debug: Run the compose status command to see which container failed. Use docker-logs for details. If the bucket is missing, check the minio-setup container output. Check that the ports are not used by something else.
